correctness.rationale: The source gives a rational surface obtained from \(\mathbb F_3\) by twelve specified blow-ups, the contact orders of the two \(t=0\) components, the ten vertical exceptional components, the horizontal sixth exceptional curves, and the two components at infinity. These data determine the full vertical lattice integrally. The checker proves that its inclusion in \(\operatorname{Pic}(S)\cong\mathbf Z^{14}\) has Smith factors \(1^{\times12},12\), so \(\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z/12\mathbf Z\). The final exceptional has fiber intersection \(1\), hence is a section; therefore the degree-zero subgroup is exactly \(J(k(t))\cong\mathbf Z/12\mathbf Z\).

value.rationale: The source presents the first known positive-characteristic genus-\(2\) semistable fibration over \(\mathbf P^1\) with four singular fibers. Determining its generic Jacobian's full Mordell–Weil group is a natural arithmetic invariant of that extremal example. The order \(12\) records the integral saturation defect of the complete vertical component lattice and is information not contained in the rank alone; it can constrain sections, divisor classes, and future comparisons of extremal four-fiber fibrations.
